paragraphs.title: The First Month and the Lord’s Command

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses and Aaron?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
An angel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.”

easy.question: Where were these words spoken to Moses and Aaron?
answers: In the wilderness
In the land of Egypt
In Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse says that they were spoken “in the land of Egypt.”

easy.question: What is this month called in the verse?
answers: The last month
The harvest month
The beginning of months
easy.explanation: The verse says, “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months.”

medium.question: What does it mean that this month is “the first month of the year”?
answers: It is the first month of the year
It is the last month of the year
It does not belong to a year
medium.explanation: The verse establishes this month as the first in the order of the months of the year.

medium.question: In the phrase “the beginning of months,” what does “beginning” mean?
answers: A leading person
The start or first place
A part of the body
medium.explanation: Here, “beginning” means the start or first place because this month opens the sequence of the year’s months.

medium.question: What is the relationship between “the beginning of months” and “the first month of the year”?
answers: Both show that this is the first month of the year
The first refers to a day and the second to an hour
They refer to two different months
medium.explanation: Both expressions repeat the same idea: this month begins the order of the year’s months.

challenge.question: What is the main purpose of declaring this month to be first?
answers: To establish a starting point for counting the months of the year
To announce that the year has ended
To establish where Moses and Aaron lived
challenge.explanation: Calling it “the beginning of months” and the first month establishes a starting point for the calendar.

challenge.question: What is especially suggested by the words “unto you”?
answers: That the month belongs only to Moses
That the month is established as first for the people being addressed
That the month is intended only for the Egyptians
challenge.explanation: “Unto you” indicates that this designation is for the Israelites, who are receiving the command.

challenge.question: What precise linguistic distinction appears in “the beginning of months”?
answers: The month is first among the months of the year
The month is the first day of the month
The month was the first thing created
challenge.explanation: The word “months” shows that “beginning” refers to the month’s position in the yearly sequence.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of declaring this month to be first?
answers: To establish a starting point for counting the months of the year
To announce that the year has ended
To establish where Moses and Aaron lived
questions.explanation: Calling it “the beginning of months” and the first month establishes a starting point for the calendar.

questions.question: What is especially suggested by the words “unto you”?
answers: That the month belongs only to Moses
That the month is established as first for the people being addressed
That the month is intended only for the Egyptians
questions.explanation: “Unto you” indicates that this designation is for the Israelites, who are receiving the command.

questions.question: What precise linguistic distinction appears in “the beginning of months”?
answers: The month is first among the months of the year
The month is the first day of the month
The month was the first thing created
questions.explanation: The word “months” shows that “beginning” refers to the month’s position in the yearly sequence.

easy.question: On which day of the month was the lamb to be taken?
answers: The tenth day of the month
The first day of the month
The end of the month
easy.explanation: The verse says, “In the tenth day of this month they shall take… a lamb.”

easy.question: What kind of lamb was acceptable?
answers: A two-year-old female
A male in its first year
Any animal without restriction
easy.explanation: The verse requires a lamb without blemish, a male in its first year.

easy.question: To whom were these instructions given?
answers: Only to the elders
Only to the priests
To all the congregation of Israel
easy.explanation: The command begins, “Speak unto all the congregation of Israel.”

medium.question: What should a household do if it is too small for one lamb?
answers: Join with its nearest neighbor
Give up the Passover sacrifice
Take two young goats
medium.explanation: A small household was to join with the neighbor nearest to its house.

medium.question: What does “according to the number of the souls” mean in this context?
answers: According to the number of houses in the street
According to the number of people eating
According to the lamb’s age
medium.explanation: The following words, “every man according to his eating,” show that the count was based on the number of people and how much they would eat.

medium.question: Why was a small household to join with its nearest neighbor?
answers: To choose a larger lamb
To live together in one house
So that the number of eaters would suit the lamb
medium.explanation: The joining was meant to match the number of people with the amount of meat in the lamb.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “a lamb according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house”?
answers: The division was according to households and families
Each person had to take a lamb
Only the father could eat the lamb
challenge.explanation: The phrase assigns a lamb to each household or family group, not to each individual.

challenge.question: What detail limits the choice of neighbor?
answers: The neighbor had to be from the same family
The neighbor had to be the one nearest the house
The neighbor had to be wealthier
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says, “his neighbour next unto his house,” not just any neighbor.

challenge.question: Which option is permitted according to the end of the passage?
answers: A one-year-old female
A three-year-old male
A perfect male lamb or goat in its first year
challenge.explanation: The verse permits an animal from the sheep or goats and requires it to be without blemish and in its first year.

questions.question: What can be understood from “a lamb according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house”?
answers: The division was according to households and families
Each person had to take a lamb
Only the father could eat the lamb
questions.explanation: The phrase assigns a lamb to each household or family group, not to each individual.

questions.question: What detail limits the choice of neighbor?
answers: The neighbor had to be from the same family
The neighbor had to be the one nearest the house
The neighbor had to be wealthier
questions.explanation: The verse specifically says, “his neighbour next unto his house,” not just any neighbor.

questions.question: Which option is permitted according to the end of the passage?
answers: A one-year-old female
A three-year-old male
A perfect male lamb or goat in its first year
questions.explanation: The verse permits an animal from the sheep or goats and requires it to be without blemish and in its first year.

paragraphs.title: Preparing the Lamb and Applying the Blood

easy.question: Where was the blood to be put?
answers: On the two side posts and the upper doorpost
On the altar only
On the eating vessels
easy.explanation: The blood was to be put on the two side posts and the upper doorpost.

easy.question: When was the Passover flesh eaten?
answers: In the morning
At night
At noon
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They shall eat the flesh in that night.”

easy.question: What was done with any meat left until morning?
answers: It was saved for the next day
It was given to the poor
It was burned with fire
easy.explanation: Anything remaining until morning was to be burned with fire.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the actions in these verses?
answers: Keep the lamb, kill it, and put its blood on the doorposts
Eat the lamb, keep it, and kill it afterward
Burn the lamb, put its ashes on the doorposts, and then eat
medium.explanation: The lamb was kept until the fourteenth day, then killed; its blood was applied to the doorway, and the meat was eaten.

medium.question: What does “keep it up” mean in this context?
answers: Give it as a gift
Keep it in safekeeping
Prepare it for a meal
medium.explanation: The lamb was kept safely for a set time, until the fourteenth day of the month.

medium.question: Which combination correctly describes how the meat was eaten?
answers: Raw, with honey and fruit
Boiled in water, with rice
Roasted with fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs
medium.explanation: The meat was to be roasted with fire and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs; eating it raw or boiled was forbidden.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from putting the blood on the two side posts and the upper doorpost?
answers: The blood marked the doorway, not the floor
The blood was placed only inside the house
The blood was spread over every wall
challenge.explanation: The side posts and upper doorpost are parts of the doorway, so the command describes marking the entrance.

challenge.question: What shows that the meal had to be prepared according to precise instructions?
answers: The whole people went out into the field
Several preparation methods were forbidden, and the meat had to be roasted
The meat could be kept for the next day
challenge.explanation: The verses specify roasting with fire and forbid eating the meat raw or boiled in water.

challenge.question: What is distinctive about the description of the killing in verse 6?
answers: One person killed all the lambs
The killing took place only after morning
The whole assembly of Israel took part at evening
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes both the time, “in the evening,” and the participation of the whole assembly.

questions.question: What can be inferred from putting the blood on the two side posts and the upper doorpost?
answers: The blood marked the doorway, not the floor
The blood was placed only inside the house
The blood was spread over every wall
questions.explanation: The side posts and upper doorpost are parts of the doorway, so the command describes marking the entrance.

questions.question: What shows that the meal had to be prepared according to precise instructions?
answers: The whole people went out into the field
Several preparation methods were forbidden, and the meat had to be roasted
The meat could be kept for the next day
questions.explanation: The verses specify roasting with fire and forbid eating the meat raw or boiled in water.

questions.question: What is distinctive about the description of the killing in verse 6?
answers: One person killed all the lambs
The killing took place only after morning
The whole assembly of Israel took part at evening
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes both the time, “in the evening,” and the participation of the whole assembly.

paragraphs.title: Eating in Haste and Protection by the Blood

easy.question: How were the Israelites to eat the Passover?
answers: Ready to leave
Sitting at ease
While sleeping
easy.explanation: They were to have their loins girded, shoes on their feet, and staff in hand, showing that they were ready to leave.

easy.question: What would the Lord do to the firstborn of Egypt?
answers: Save them all
Strike them
Send them into the wilderness
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.”

easy.question: What was the blood on the houses intended to do?
answers: Decorate the houses
Mark the place of the meal
Serve as a sign protecting those inside
easy.explanation: The blood would be a sign; when the Lord saw it, He would pass over the house and prevent the plague from striking it.

medium.question: What can be understood from eating with loins girded, shoes on, and a staff in hand?
answers: The people had to be ready to leave quickly
The people had to remain home for a long time
The people were preparing for a hunting trip
medium.explanation: These details show that the Israelites had to be prepared for immediate departure.

medium.question: What does “in haste” mean in this context?
answers: With great joy
Quickly and urgently
In complete silence
medium.explanation: The clothing and staff show that they were to eat quickly because their departure was near and urgent.

medium.question: What is the order of events in verse 13?
answers: The blood is seen, the Lord passes over, and there is no plague
The people leave, and then put blood on the houses
The Lord strikes Israel, and then sees the blood
medium.explanation: The blood is on the houses; the Lord sees it and passes over them, so the plague does not strike them.

challenge.question: According to the verses, what distinguished the Israelite houses from the Egyptian houses?
answers: Blood was on the Israelite houses
The Israelite houses were larger
The Israelites ate during the day
challenge.explanation: The blood was a sign on the Israelite houses, so the Lord passed over and protected them.

challenge.question: What does “both man and beast” show about the plague in Egypt?
answers: It affected only people
It included the firstborn of both people and animals
It affected only animals
challenge.explanation: The phrase covers a wide range—from human beings to animals—and includes both kinds of firstborn.

challenge.question: What idea connects eating in haste with the plague of the firstborn?
answers: Both events happened only in the morning
Both were lessons about farming
It was a night of departure, protection, and judgment
challenge.explanation: The Israelites ate ready to leave, while that same night the Lord judged Egypt and protected the houses marked with blood.

questions.question: According to the verses, what distinguished the Israelite houses from the Egyptian houses?
answers: Blood was on the Israelite houses
The Israelite houses were larger
The Israelites ate during the day
questions.explanation: The blood was a sign on the Israelite houses, so the Lord passed over and protected them.

questions.question: What does “both man and beast” show about the plague in Egypt?
answers: It affected only people
It included the firstborn of both people and animals
It affected only animals
questions.explanation: The phrase covers a wide range—from human beings to animals—and includes both kinds of firstborn.

questions.question: What idea connects eating in haste with the plague of the firstborn?
answers: Both events happened only in the morning
Both were lessons about farming
It was a night of departure, protection, and judgment
questions.explanation: The Israelites ate ready to leave, while that same night the Lord judged Egypt and protected the houses marked with blood.

paragraphs.title: The Passover Feast for Future Generations

easy.question: What would this day be for the people?
answers: A memorial
A war
A market day
easy.explanation: The verse says that the day would be a memorial.

easy.question: For whom were they to keep the feast?
answers: Moses
The Lord
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall keep it a feast to the Lord.”

easy.question: For how many generations was the feast to be kept?
answers: Only one generation
Two generations
Your generations
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the feast be kept throughout their generations.

medium.question: What is the relationship between remembrance and celebration in the verse?
answers: Celebration helps preserve the remembrance
Remembrance cancels the celebration
They are unrelated
medium.explanation: The day is intended both as a memorial and as a feast, so celebrating helps preserve its memory.

medium.question: What does “an ordinance for ever” mean?
answers: A one-time custom
A lasting command
A feast lasting one day
medium.explanation: In this context, it means a fixed command to be observed continually.

medium.question: What follows from the words “throughout your generations”?
answers: The feast belongs only to the past
The feast is only for leaders
The feast must continue in future generations
medium.explanation: The command extends to the generations that follow.

challenge.question: Which combination of purposes for the day appears in the verse?
answers: Remembrance and celebration
War and trade
Study and work
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the day is for remembrance and that it is to be kept as a feast to the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from repeating the idea of celebrating the feast at the end?
answers: The feast was canceled
The duty to celebrate is emphasized and continues
The feast is only for one day
challenge.explanation: The repeated command, together with “an ordinance for ever,” emphasizes its importance and continuity.

challenge.question: What is the main significance of “this” in “this day”?
answers: An unspecified day
A day that will occur only in the future
A specific day to remember and celebrate
challenge.explanation: “This” points to a particular day that the verse establishes as a memorial and feast.

questions.question: Which combination of purposes for the day appears in the verse?
answers: Remembrance and celebration
War and trade
Study and work
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the day is for remembrance and that it is to be kept as a feast to the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from repeating the idea of celebrating the feast at the end?
answers: The feast was canceled
The duty to celebrate is emphasized and continues
The feast is only for one day
questions.explanation: The repeated command, together with “an ordinance for ever,” emphasizes its importance and continuity.

questions.question: What is the main significance of “this” in “this day”?
answers: An unspecified day
A day that will occur only in the future
A specific day to remember and celebrate
questions.explanation: “This” points to a particular day that the verse establishes as a memorial and feast.

easy.question: How many days were they commanded to eat unleavened bread?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread.”

easy.question: On which days was there to be a holy convocation?
answers: The second and sixth days
The first and seventh days
All seven days
easy.explanation: The verse specifically names the first day and the seventh day.

easy.question: What was not to be found in the houses during the seven days?
answers: Unleavened bread
Water
Leaven
easy.explanation: The command says that no leaven was to be found in the houses.

medium.question: What had to be done on the first day concerning leaven?
answers: Leaven had to be put away from the houses
Leavened bread had to be eaten at night
People had to work as usual
medium.explanation: On the first day, the Israelites were commanded to remove leaven; during the seven days they were not to eat leavened bread.

medium.question: What does “put away” mean in “put away leaven out of your houses”?
answers: Cook it
Remove it or stop keeping it
Save it
medium.explanation: The context shows that leaven was to be removed from the houses and no longer kept there.

medium.question: What work was permitted on the holy days?
answers: All farm work
Commercial work
Preparing food
medium.explanation: Most work was forbidden, but work necessary for preparing food was permitted.

challenge.question: How should the period from the evening of the fourteenth day to the evening of the twenty-first day be understood?
answers: It includes seven days of eating unleavened bread
It includes only one day
It begins on the morning of the fifteenth day
challenge.explanation: The verses count the period from the evening of the fourteenth to the evening of the twenty-first, corresponding to seven days.

challenge.question: What does the mention of “a stranger, or born in the land” show about the prohibition of leaven?
answers: It applies only to priests
It applies both to the stranger and to the native-born
The stranger may eat leaven
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the prohibition applies both to the resident foreigner and to one born in the land.

challenge.question: Why was food preparation permitted even though work was forbidden?
answers: The first day was not a holy day
Only work outside the house was forbidden
The verse permits work needed for food
challenge.explanation: The phrase “save that which every man must eat” creates an exception for preparing food.

questions.question: How should the period from the evening of the fourteenth day to the evening of the twenty-first day be understood?
answers: It includes seven days of eating unleavened bread
It includes only one day
It begins on the morning of the fifteenth day
questions.explanation: The verses count the period from the evening of the fourteenth to the evening of the twenty-first, corresponding to seven days.

questions.question: What does the mention of “a stranger, or born in the land” show about the prohibition of leaven?
answers: It applies only to priests
It applies both to the stranger and to the native-born
The stranger may eat leaven
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the prohibition applies both to the resident foreigner and to one born in the land.

questions.question: Why was food preparation permitted even though work was forbidden?
answers: The first day was not a holy day
Only work outside the house was forbidden
The verse permits work needed for food
questions.explanation: The phrase “save that which every man must eat” creates an exception for preparing food.

easy.question: Whom did Moses call to deliver the instructions?
answers: The elders of Israel
The kings of Egypt
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses called for all the elders of Israel.”

easy.question: Where was the blood to be placed?
answers: On the floor only
On the upper doorpost and the two side posts
On the roof
easy.explanation: The blood was to be placed on the upper doorpost and the two side posts.

easy.question: Until when were the Israelites commanded not to leave their houses?
answers: Until evening
Until noon
Until morning
easy.explanation: The command says that no one was to go out of his house until morning.

medium.question: What was the result of the blood on the upper doorpost and side posts?
answers: The destroyer did not enter the houses
The houses became larger
The Israelites left Egypt immediately
medium.explanation: The blood was a sign, so the Lord passed over the door and did not allow the destroyer to enter and strike the house.

medium.question: Which order of actions matches the instructions?
answers: Leave the house, take a lamb, and then apply blood
Take a lamb, kill the Passover, dip hyssop in the blood, and apply it to the doorway
Apply blood first, then decide whether to take a lamb
medium.explanation: They first took and killed the lamb, then dipped hyssop in the blood and applied it to the upper doorpost and side posts.

medium.question: What does “a bunch” mean in “a bunch of hyssop”?
answers: A gate or door
An earthen vessel
A bundle tied together
medium.explanation: The context indicates a bundle of hyssop that could be dipped in blood and used to reach the doorway.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Moses giving the instructions to the elders?
answers: The elders were to pass the instructions on to the families
Only the elders were to offer the Passover
The children were unrelated to the instructions
challenge.explanation: Moses addressed the elders as representatives of the people, while the instructions were intended for every household.

challenge.question: Which precise detail about the location of the blood is easy to miss?
answers: It was placed only on the right side post
It was placed on the upper doorpost and both side posts
It was placed only on the threshold
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes all three locations: the upper doorpost and the two side posts.

challenge.question: What does the command to observe this ordinance forever teach?
answers: The command was only for that night
The command was only for the elders
The command was also to be kept by future generations
challenge.explanation: The references to the sons and to keeping it forever show that the command was not temporary.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Moses giving the instructions to the elders?
answers: The elders were to pass the instructions on to the families
Only the elders were to offer the Passover
The children were unrelated to the instructions
questions.explanation: Moses addressed the elders as representatives of the people, while the instructions were intended for every household.

questions.question: Which precise detail about the location of the blood is easy to miss?
answers: It was placed only on the right side post
It was placed on the upper doorpost and both side posts
It was placed only on the threshold
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes all three locations: the upper doorpost and the two side posts.

questions.question: What does the command to observe this ordinance forever teach?
answers: The command was only for that night
The command was only for the elders
The command was also to be kept by future generations
questions.explanation: The references to the sons and to keeping it forever show that the command was not temporary.

paragraphs.title: The Passover Tradition and the Plague in Egypt

easy.question: What would the Israelites observe when they came into the land?
answers: This service
Pharaoh’s palace
The prison house
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall keep this service.”

easy.question: What would the children ask their parents?
answers: Who was Moses?
What mean ye by this service?
When will we reach the land?
easy.explanation: The children would ask, “What mean ye by this service?”

easy.question: What happened to Egypt’s firstborn at midnight?
answers: They left Egypt
They bowed down
The Lord struck them
easy.explanation: At midnight, the Lord struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites explain the Passover sacrifice to their children?
answers: To explain that the Lord saved the Israelite houses in Egypt
To teach them to build houses
To tell them about Pharaoh’s kingdom
medium.explanation: The explanation recalls that the Lord passed over the Israelite houses and delivered them when He struck Egypt.

medium.question: What did the Israelites do after receiving the command from Moses and Aaron?
answers: They questioned Pharaoh
They did as they were commanded
They immediately left Egypt
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Israelites did exactly as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron.

medium.question: What does “struck” mean in the context of striking Egypt?
answers: Blessed Egypt
Left Egypt
Hit and afflicted Egypt
medium.explanation: The context describes the plague of the firstborn, so “struck” means hit or afflicted.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “from the firstborn of Pharaoh… unto the firstborn of the captive”?
answers: The plague affected firstborn across every level of society
Only Pharaoh’s family was affected
Only prisoners were affected
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both Pharaoh’s firstborn and the captive’s firstborn emphasizes that every level of Egyptian society was affected.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the Passover sacrifice and the plague of the firstborn?
answers: The sacrifice caused the plague
The sacrifice commemorates the saving of the Israelite houses during the plague
The sacrifice celebrates the death of all firstborn
challenge.explanation: The passage explains that the sacrifice recalls how the Lord passed over and delivered the Israelite houses when He struck Egypt.

challenge.question: What does the great cry in Egypt emphasize?
answers: All the Egyptians went to war
The Israelites asked many questions
The disaster was widespread, with no house without a dead person
challenge.explanation: The verse says there was no house in Egypt without someone dead, so there was a great cry throughout the land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “from the firstborn of Pharaoh… unto the firstborn of the captive”?
answers: The plague affected firstborn across every level of society
Only Pharaoh’s family was affected
Only prisoners were affected
questions.explanation: Mentioning both Pharaoh’s firstborn and the captive’s firstborn emphasizes that every level of Egyptian society was affected.

answers: The sacrifice caused the plague

The sacrifice celebrates the death of all firstborn
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the sacrifice recalls how the Lord passed over and delivered the Israelite houses when He struck Egypt.

answers: All the Egyptians went to war
The Israelites asked many questions
The disaster was widespread, with no house without a dead person
questions.explanation: The verse says there was no house in Egypt without someone dead, so there was a great cry throughout the land.

easy.question: Whom did Pharaoh call during the night?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Joshua and Caleb
The elders of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron by night.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command the Israelites to do?
answers: Remain in Egypt
Leave and serve the Lord
Return to Canaan
easy.explanation: Pharaoh said, “Rise up, and get you forth… and go, serve the Lord.”

easy.question: Which animals were the Israelites allowed to take?
answers: Donkeys and camels
Doves and fish
Flocks and herds
easy.explanation: Pharaoh said, “Also take your flocks and your herds.”

medium.question: Why did the Egyptians urge the Israelites to leave?
answers: They said, “We are all dead men”
They wanted to leave with them
Moses requested it
medium.explanation: The Egyptians feared further death and said, “We be all dead men,” so they hurried to send Israel away.

medium.question: What did Pharaoh ask of the Israelites after telling them to take their flocks and herds?
answers: That they remain in Egypt
That they bless him also
That they give him their cattle
medium.explanation: After telling them to go with their possessions, Pharaoh said, “And bless me also.”

medium.question: What does “were urgent upon” mean in this context?
answers: Blessed
Protected
Pressured and hurried
medium.explanation: The Egyptians hurried the Israelites out, so the phrase means that they pressured and urged them to leave.

challenge.question: To whom does “both ye” refer in Pharaoh’s words?
answers: Moses and Aaron
All the Egyptians
The Israelite children only
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh first addressed Moses and Aaron, so “both ye” refers to them, in addition to the Israelites.

challenge.question: What is implied by “as ye have said” concerning the flocks and herds?
answers: They had previously given them up
They had already asked to take them
They had received them from the Egyptians
challenge.explanation: The words show that taking the flocks and herds had already been included in their earlier request.

challenge.question: Who said, “We be all dead men”?
answers: The Israelites
Moses and Aaron
The Egyptians
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Egyptians hurried to send the people away because they said, “We be all dead men.”

questions.question: To whom does “both ye” refer in Pharaoh’s words?
answers: Moses and Aaron
All the Egyptians
The Israelite children only
questions.explanation: Pharaoh first addressed Moses and Aaron, so “both ye” refers to them, in addition to the Israelites.

questions.question: What is implied by “as ye have said” concerning the flocks and herds?
answers: They had previously given them up

They had received them from the Egyptians
questions.explanation: The words show that taking the flocks and herds had already been included in their earlier request.

questions.question: Who said, “We be all dead men”?
answers: The Israelites
Moses and Aaron
The Egyptians
questions.explanation: The verse says that the Egyptians hurried to send the people away because they said, “We be all dead men.”

paragraphs.title: The Dough and the Wealth from Egypt

easy.question: What did the Israelites carry before leaving Egypt?
answers: Their dough
Their tents
The vessels of the sanctuary
